text: In this video, we'll install OpenCrabs on Ubuntu with a single paste, from zero to your first chat.
Open a terminal. On the Ubuntu desktop, press Control, Alt and T.
Next, one line so OpenCrabs never has to stop and ask for your password. Copy it from the description, paste it, and press Enter.
Ubuntu asks for your password one last time. Nothing appears while you type it. That's normal. Type it and press Enter.
Already logged in as root, on a server for example? Skip this line and paste the install block as it is.
Now the whole install is one paste. Copy this block from the docs or the description, paste it into the terminal, and press Enter.
On an ARM machine, copy the arm64 block from the docs instead. It's the same, with arm64 in the file name.
This time there's no password prompt. It does everything in one go. It installs three small helpers, finds the newest release, downloads it, and starts OpenCrabs.
If you see gzip, unexpected end of file, here instead, the version lookup came back empty. Wait a moment, then paste the block again.
If it stops at libgomp dot so dot one, cannot open shared object file, the helpers didn't install. Paste the block again.
The setup wizard opens. Choose QuickStart, the sensible defaults, and press Enter.

Home Base is the dot opencrabs folder in your home directory. That's always the default. Keep Seed template files ticked. We recommend it: those files give your crab its personality, so you start with the complete crab. You can change them later if you want. Press Enter.
Brain Fuel is the important one. Pick your AI provider. We'll use Z dot A I with GLM models. It costs far less than most, and coding plans are supported.
If you're on a GLM coding plan, set Endpoint Type to Coding API. Then paste your API key. It's hidden on screen. Never share your key with anyone.
Keep the default model, or pick another one, and press Enter.
Always On can keep OpenCrabs running in the background. Skip it for now. There's a separate video for that.
Vibe Check makes sure everything is wired up. All OK? Press Enter.
Make It Yours lets you tell OpenCrabs about yourself. Press Escape to skip it for now.
Setup complete. And you're in.
You don't even type first. Your crab says hello on its own. Every crab opens differently, but that's it. OpenCrabs is installed and running.
Next time, start it the same way. Open a terminal in your home folder, and type dot slash opencrabs, then press Enter.
Every command from this video is in the description, ready to copy.
Next up: keep OpenCrabs running in the background, and connect it to Telegram so you can chat from your phone. See you there.
